column1: If the central bank can conduct open market operations in an asset that is an imperfect substitute for money, monetary policy can still affect inflation, even in a liquidity trap. McCallum (2000) and Svensson (2001), for example, argued that a central bank can generate inflation by depreciating its currency, and Goodfriend (2000) considered the effects of open market operations in long-term bonds. By increasing the equilibrium price level, and thereby causing private agents to expect a positive rate of inflation, such policies can prevent nominal interest rates from falling to zero.
